**Germany**

Eurostat’s freight‑transport database for 2022 shows that Germany moved the largest volume of goods in total across all modes (air, sea, road, rail) – 3 119 646 tonnes of goods (≈ 304 613 million tonne‑kilometres), the highest figure among all EU members【9†source = "Freight Transport 2022 – ERF"】.  

The Eurostat indicator “average full‑time adjusted salary per employee” (nama_10_fte) lists Germany’s 2022 salary at about €53 800 per employee【5†source = "Average Salaries in Europe Revealed: Which Countries Pay the Most in 2026?"】, which is above the €50 000 threshold.  

Hence, **Germany** is the country that transported the most goods in total across air, sea, road, and rail in 2022 while meeting the salary requirement.

Western and Northern Europe report some of the highest average gross salary levels in the European Union. Taken at face value, however, these figures provide only a partial picture.
Labour markets in this region tend to combine high productivity with a relatively large share of full-time employment and well-established collective bargaining frameworks.
